fr.elements: Main Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Internal Drive Aisle; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Landscaped Area; Dumpster Enclosure; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Single Access Point; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Mark each access point with visible signage identifying it by name or number to help responders navigate to the correct entry during an emergency.

• Post the building address or identifier at the primary street frontage in characters large enough to be read from a moving vehicle.

• Keep the internal drive aisle clear of parked vehicles and other obstructions to allow emergency vehicles to move through the property without stopping.

• Mark the single access point serving the rear of the property with reflective signage so responders can locate it quickly under low-visibility conditions.

• Keep the dumpster enclosure and surrounding area clear of overflow materials that could block the drive aisle or obstruct emergency vehicle movement.

• Keep the walkway connecting the parking area to the building entrance clear to allow unobstructed movement by responders on foot.

wildfire.conditions: Large Paved Area; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Landscaped Island; Scattered Trees; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin shrubs that are concentrated near building entrances or walls to keep plant material away from structures.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from landscaped islands located within the paved area.
• Trim lower branches from scattered trees near buildings to keep foliage off walls and rooflines.
• Keep the large paved area free of vegetation encroachment along its edges to maintain clear movement for vehicles and responders.
• Maintain all access routes clear of overhanging branches and vegetation crowding the travel lanes.
